Ensure the email is sent before the last date: 20-09-2026. Keep a copy of the sent email for future reference.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for the IIT Patna JRF position?
faq.answer: The last date to submit your application via email for the Junior Research Fellow position at IIT Patna is 20th September 2026.

faq.question: Q2. What is the educational qualification required for the JRF post?
faq.answer: Candidates must have an M.Sc/M.Tech/M.E./M.Phil./B.Tech./B.E. with a minimum CPI of 6.5 out of 10 or 60% marks, along with a CSIR/UGC-NET or valid GATE score.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for the Junior Research Fellow position?
faq.answer: The maximum age limit is 28 years for M.Sc./B.Tech./B.E. and 32 years for M.Tech./M.E./M.Phil. Age relaxations are applicable as per GOI rules.

faq.question: Q4. How will candidates be selected for the JRF role?
faq.answer: The selection process involves shortlisting candidates based on their eligibility and then conducting an interview, which can be either online or offline.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary offered for the Junior Research Fellow position?
faq.answer: The selected candidate will receive a monthly salary of Rs. 37,000/- along with House Rent Allowance (HRA) as per the norms.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application mode for this recruitment?
faq.answer: Applications are to be submitted via email to the specified address. No other mode of application will be accepted.

faq.question: Q7. Is there any application fee for the IIT Patna JRF recruitment?
faq.answer: The official notification does not mention any specific application fee for this recruitment drive.

faq.question: Q8. What is the advertisement number for this recruitment?
faq.answer: The advertisement number for this recruitment is R&D/1227/MQR/622.

faq.question: Q9. What is the total number of vacancies available?
faq.answer: There is one vacancy for the post of Junior Research Fellow (JRF) at IIT Patna.

faq.question: Q10. Are there any preferences for certain candidates?
faq.answer: Yes, candidates with working/research experience in Quantum Optics and Light-matter experiments, and those who studied physics as a major subject in their UG/PG degree, will be given preference.
